content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Synthetic probe alert fired for /healthcheck in eu-west-1 (probe-runner-43). 5xx rate increased above threshold (15m window). Severity: P2.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: page triggered -> OnCall: @ops-oncall. Incident ID: PD-88421. Escalation policy: synthetic-checks.
ops-oncall: Acked on PD. I'm looking at the probe dashboard now, pulling last 30m.
sara: I'm seeing a small spike in probe failures starting ~+00:04:30. Total failed probes: 42/300 in the last 15m. Linking probe histogram: https://grafana.redwood/s/probes/eu-health
mike: Any deploys to binary-search service in the last hour? I don't see a runtime deploy in CI.
jess: No deploys on prod in the last hour from the releases channel. Checked deploy bot: no tags.
vijay: Reading prober logs - hitting 503s with connection reset on keepalive. Suspect a backend pool exhaustion or recent config push. Log sample: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:27Z] probe_id=43 url=/healthcheck status=503 backend=bs-12 conn_err=EOF rt=312ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] probe_id=43 url=/healthcheck status=200 backend=bs-12 rt=98ms
[2026-03-15T10:13:01Z] probe_id=43 url=/healthcheck status=503 backend=bs-12 conn_err=timeout rt=5001ms
```
ops-oncall: Good catch. Is this localized to bs-12 pool or wider?
sara: Filtered by backend tag: failures concentrated on bs-12 (IP range 10.80.12.*). Other pools show nominal success rates.
mike: bs-12 is one of the new autoscaled pools behind the routing change rolled out ~2h ago. Could be insufficient capacity at longer tails.
vijay: Checking instance-level logs for bs-12. I'm seeing repeated OOM killer events on instance i-0a3b2c: ```
Mar 15 10:11:58 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4723 (worker) score 112
Mar 15 10:12:00 systemd: service worker restarted (OOM)
```
jess: If OOM is happening, probes would see transient 5xx until instance restarts. Any recent change to memory limits? Eng-runtime?
mike: We rolled a config last night reducing memory reservation on worker container to free headroom for batch jobs. That may explain it. Reverting will help but needs a canary.
ops-oncall: Immediate mitigation: temporarily mark bs-12 pool as unhealthy in routing to stop probes hitting it. I'll run the routing disable command, then monitor.
ops-oncall: ```bash
# disable bs-12 pool from the probe routing map
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RDW_OPS' https://api.redwood.internal/routing/pools/bs-12/disable
```
vijay: I disabled bs-12 at 10:14:05Z (routing API returned 200). Traffic should drain in ~30s.
sara: After disable, probe failures dropped back to baseline within 90s. Current failed probes 3/320 in last 15m. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty-bot: PD update: incident acknowledged and mitigated. Please post a short postmortem link when available.
mike: I'll open a revert PR to restore the previous memory reservation and schedule a controlled canary to bs-12 after it's applied. tagging @eng-runtime for verification.
jess: For the follow-up, let's capture: root cause = lowered memory reservation causing OOMs on bs-12; mitigation = routed probes away + revert config; action items = revert PR, improve monitoring alert (OOM rate), add preflight check for memory reservation changes.
ops-oncall: Handoff to night oncall at 2026-03-15T22:00Z. Night oncall - please monitor probe success rate for eu-west-1 for 2 hours post-revert.
vijay: Created PD follow-up task PD-88421-1 and a GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/4021. I'll attach logs and instance IDs.
sara: Thanks everyone. Closing the page. If anything regresses, re-open PD and ping this thread. :handshake:
